newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arafat demands new PLO-Israel economic accord.
newsitem.headline: Arafat demands new PLO-Israel economic accord.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, accusing Israel of violating a 1994 economic agreement between the PLO and the Jewish state, demanded on Wednesday that it be rewritten.

Addressing a World Bank donors' meeting on the West Bank and Gaza, Arafat said Israel's decision to close off the Palestinian territories in February after a wave of bomb attacks by Moslem fundamentalists had weighed heavily on the Palestinian economy.

Arafat said the accord was based on two principles -- a Palestinian workforce in Israel that was 90,000 strong in 1993, and freedom of movement for individuals and goods to and from Gaza and the West Bank.

"For the last 30 months, Israel has violated this accord through deliberate methods, procedural devices and decisions that strip the accord of its meaning, form and content," Arafat said in a speech released by the PLO's Paris office.

"That is why we demand that the accord be rewritten in line with our joint commitments which provide for the right to revise the accord since May 4, 1995, something which Israel has always evaded," he said.

Arafat said a revised accord must force Israel to lift restrictions and quotas on direct imports by the Palestinians, transfer sales tax revenue collected by the Israeli treasury and recognise Palestinian technical standards.
